summary: Obfuscated agent daemon exposes installer host to remote shell/PTY via author-controlled WebSocket gateway
details: The package installs a long-running daemon (`bin: whalent` -> `dist/index.cjs`) that dials out to a WebSocket gateway (default `memory.whalent.com`, overridable via `--gateway`) and, per the README, `accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway`. The declared runtime dependencies (`ws`, `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, `ssh2`) are the shape of a remote-terminal/agent runner: bytes arriving on the gateway websocket drive shell/PTY sessions on the host running the daemon, giving the gateway operator interactive command execution on that host. Both `dist/index.cjs` (~131 KB) and `dist/core.cjs` (~13 MB) are fully wrapped with javascript-obfuscator (string-array bootstrap, `_0x...` hex identifiers, control-flow flattening; `javascript-obfuscator` is present in devDependencies), which prevents inspection of exactly which gateway messages map to which local exec paths, what authentication/authorization exists on the control channel, and whether any behavior falls outside the advertised upgrade/restart surface. The daemon only runs when the user explicitly starts `whalent` (no lifecycle hook, no `require`-time side effect), so this is not install-time RCE — but once started, the host is under remote control of whoever operates the configured gateway, and the default gateway is author-controlled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
